public_rationale: The factual core holds. In the weeks before the post, leading AI labs were raising money at much higher valuations. On January 30, 2025, Reuters reported that SoftBank valued OpenAI at $260 billion going into a round at up to $300 billion, up from $150 billion a few months earlier (e2). On February 14, 2025, Bloomberg, relayed by Reuters, reported xAI in talks at about $75 billion, against a prior $40 billion (e1). Anthropic then closed a round at $61.5 billion on March 3 (e3, context). The 'results notwithstanding' part is the author's opinion about whether the valuations are deserved. It is not graded.
limitations: The supporting figures come from talks reported by anonymous sources, not closed rounds.
The claim names no companies. Public-market AI stocks were more volatile in this period.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI valuations just keep rising regardless of the results, at least for now.

statement.excerpt: Instead, valuations just keep rising, results notwithstanding.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: the valuations of leading AI companies (such as OpenAI, xAI and Anthropic) in private funding rounds were still going up around the time of the post.
'Results notwithstanding' is the author's judgment that the models' results do not justify those valuations. It is opinion and is not graded.
Target period: the weeks before the post (2025-01-01 to 2025-02-19), the most recent period public reporting could cover when he wrote 'now'.
criteria.support_condition: Reported funding rounds or talks in early 2025 value leading AI labs above their previous valuations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reported rounds in early 2025 show flat or lower valuations (down rounds) for leading AI labs.
